chunks: They shall have what they wish from their Lord. This is the recompense for the good.

key_terms.الْمُحْسِنِينَ: The doers of good / The righteous

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for the righteous in Paradise according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Az-Zumar is often linked with the preceding verse (39:33) to distinguish between the 'Muhsinun' (those who do good with faith and sincerity) and the 'Muhsinat' (women who do good), highlighting that divine reward is tailored to individual capacity and desire. Scholars emphasize that 'what they wish for' includes not only physical pleasures but also the spiritual joy of beholding the Divine Face, reflecting the concept of 'Jaza' based on 'Amal' (reward corresponding to deed). This underscores the infinite generosity of Allah, who grants the righteous more than they can even conceive, fulfilling both their worldly and otherworldly aspirations.
